results.title: Fish Audio Launches Drama 3 to Direct AI Voices and Edit a Single Word – Unite.AI
results.content:
The company’s claims address both problems, but the practical test will be the finished scene: listeners should not hear abrupt changes in identity or delivery when speakers switch, a passage is edited, or the script changes language.

## Where Drama 3 Fits in Fish Audio’s Technology

The direction-first approach builds on a research path Fish Audio has already described. Its earlier S2 research release supported natural-language instructions embedded at specific word or phrase positions. The company described a dual-autoregressive architecture that separates prediction along the audio timeline from generation of finer acoustic detail, alongside reinforcement-learning alignment for intelligibility, instruction adherence, and voice similarity. [...] Fish Audio is targeting those production problems with Drama 3, its new text-to-speech model announced on October 13. The company says creators can direct delivery in ordinary language, generate scenes with multiple speakers, and repair a selected segment of synthesized audio without regenerating the surrounding performance.

The most consequential feature may be the smallest edit: changing a single word while preserving the voice, mood, and rhythm on either side. For teams building audiobooks, dubbed content, games, or audio dramas, the value of a synthetic voice increasingly depends on how easily it can be revised.

## Giving a Voice Performance Direction [...] ## Audio Inpainting: Fixing the Moment That Fails

Fish Audio describes Drama 3’s audio inpainting as a way to select a portion of an existing performance, update the instructions, and regenerate that segment while retaining the surrounding audio. Co-founder and chief scientist Shijia Liao says the model uses the sound on both sides of an edited word to make the replacement fit.

That is a different task from generating an isolated replacement line. The new audio has to connect to an established performance: its timing, intonation, and vocal identity all need to remain believable at the boundaries of the edit.

One version sounds like a casual conversation. The other sounds like a professional tutorial. And the interesting part? You can literally direct the performance inside the script, right down to specific words. I recorded the whole process. Listen to the difference.
